tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy COLD-SEASON single-column run, data/eqwefic/noahcold_scm, dumped by ctessum-claude/WRF branch earthsciml-instrumented-noahcold and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) kernels/noah_driver at ESM_DT = 60 s, WRF's OWN step; tolerances are the 1e-9 that a double-precision kernel build earns. WHY THE LARGEST STEP AND NOT THE SMALLEST. SNOWPACK is not a rate: Koren's solution is a closed form in the step length, so the density increment is proportional to dtsec and there is no dt -> 0 limit to approach by shrinking the step. Nothing here is formed as a difference either -- the increment is written as sndens_in pexp_m1 + dw (1 - dsx), an exact rearrangement in which nothing cancels, and its reference comes from a publisher that emits the Taylor series BEFORE WRF adds one to it (FORTRAN_BUGS N99) -- so there is no cancellation floor pushing the step DOWN either. What is left is that a smaller step puts LESS of the assertion's budget on the physics: at 60 s the compaction and retention move the density by 4.5e-9 to 9.4e-5 of itself, so a rel 1e-9 assertion on sndens_out tests them to between 1e-5 and 2e-1 of themselves, while at 1e-6 s the same assertion would test them to nothing at all -- the increment is 7.5e-17 of the density there. This is the fifth distinct direction the Noah reference step has had to move (surface closure 1e-6 s, tendencies 1e-2 s, runoff 1e-4 s, canopy drip 1e-2 s, compaction 60 s), and it is why the choice is argued per quantity rather than assumed. The companion regime at 1e-6 s pins the tendency in the dt -> 0 limit. Step 26 of case A, snow falling onto initially bare frozen ground. dry branch -- the snow surface is below freezing and only compaction acts; the pack is below the esdcx floor, so the compaction argument uses the floored 0.01 cm while the depth diagnostic keeps the true water equivalent; neither density limit fires. The density moves by 7.794e-08 of itself over the step.
